name: Black Mariah
description: Black Mariah is an umbrella name for several Seven Card Stud poker variants that all revolve around the Queen of Spades or spades in general. In the most distinctive version, a player must hold BOTH the best poker hand AND the highest spade at showdown to win the pot. If those two conditions are met by different players, or if no one holds spades, nobody wins and the pot carries over â€” making it a potentially monster pot that grows across multiple deals.

history.origins: Black Mariah emerged from American home poker games as one of several Seven Card Stud variants using the Queen of Spades (Qâ™ ) or spades generally as a special mechanic. The name 'Black Mariah' (or 'Maria') is also used in Hearts to refer to the Qâ™ . The poker variant shares this dramatic association.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Stud poker variants with special card mechanics emerge in American home games.
Late 20th century: Black Mariah becomes a staple of dealer's-choice home poker nights alongside Chicago and The Bitch.
Present: Primarily a home/casual game â€” the multiple definitions under the same name reflect its folk-game nature.
history.cultural: The Qâ™  as 'Mariah' or 'Maria' is one of the most culturally loaded cards in Western card games, featured in Hearts (penalty card), Bridge lore, and multiple poker variants.
history.evolution: The name Black Mariah is used for at least four different stud variants, showing the oral-tradition nature of home poker game evolution.

setup.players: Two to eight players. This version of Black Mariah is a seven card stud variant; as in standard stud, the usual number is two to eight so that each player receives seven cards from a single 52-card deck. Only players who were in the showdown participate in the next deal when the pot has carried over.
setup.dealing: Standard Seven Card Stud deal: 2 cards face-down, 4 face-up, 1 face-down. Betting rounds after each up-card.

rules.objective: Win the pot by holding BOTH the best 5-card poker hand AND the highest spade among all players at showdown.
rules.gameplay: Seven card stud deal: two cards face down, four face up, one face down. Five betting rounds, one after each round of face-up cards and one after the final card. At showdown, to win the pot a player must have both the best five-card poker hand and the highest spade among all players; the highest spade may be any of the seven cards, not necessarily face down. If the best hand and the highest spade are held by different players, or if no one has a spade, no one wins and the pot carries over to the next deal. Only players who were in the showdown participate in the carryover deal.
keyRules: Must hold BOTH best hand AND highest spade to win.
If conditions are split between players, pot carries over.
Carried-over pot grows across multiple deals â€” can become enormous.
Only showdown participants play the next deal when pot carries over.
Highest spade uses ANY of the 7 cards, not just hole cards.

strategy.basic: Value spades highly. A hand with the Ace of Spades in the hole is extremely powerful â€” it guarantees the highest-spade requirement. Focus on building the best hand while holding strong spades.
strategy.intermediate: Track spades on the board: if the Aâ™  is visible in someone's up-cards, they have a huge advantage. If most high spades are mucked or visible, estimate which spades remain in play. With no spades in your hand, you literally cannot win â€” fold unless you can improve.
strategy.advanced: The carryover mechanic changes strategy dramatically when the pot is large. Players with high spades in the hole should play aggressively to build a monster pot they can scoop. Monitor opponents' visible spades to assess whether the pot will likely carry over or be claimed.
tips: Aâ™  in the hole is nearly unbeatable for the spade requirement â€” play aggressively.
With no spades in hand by 5th street, folding is usually correct.
Multiple carryovers create massive pots â€” the game becomes very high-stakes quickly.
Track all visible spades carefully to estimate your spade's ranking.

scoring.description: Standard poker pot. Pot only awarded when one player satisfies both conditions. Unclaimed pots carry forward.
scoring.winCondition: Best hand + highest spade = win. Split = carryover.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Seven Card Stud variant where you must hold BOTH the best poker hand and the highest spade to claim the pot. If different players hold each, nobody wins and the pot carries over â€” growing larger and more dangerous with each unclaimed round.
